progress.text: Tracks and Groups and the Clip List sit in dock columns that run the Edit window's full height at its left and right edges, with the MIDI Editor under the session view between them; Mix docks Tracks and Groups at its left edge. A panel dragged onto a dock group joins it as a tab, stacks above or below it, or makes a new column; one dragged to an empty window edge makes a dock there. A list with no saved place reopens in its dock, and makes the dock again when it is gone. Preferences and window configurations saved with the earlier split-frame layouts load with the new default layouts and keep their other settings. No readiness percentage change.

Auto Pan moves the balance of a stereo track: the left channel's level falls as the position moves right and the right channel's as it moves left, at constant power, and each channel stays on its own side. At the center the track passes unchanged, so a wide or out-of-phase stereo image keeps its width, and the envelope follower follows the louder channel. No readiness percentage change.

Clip List › Auto Rename (clip.autorename) sets the names that editing gives the clips it separates from the selected clips: a name, a starting number, a number of places (zeros before the number) and a suffix. The piece after each cut takes the next name, the piece before it keeps its name, and all the pieces count up one number sequence. Pieces that Strip Silence names with its own Rename fields, or removes, take no Auto Rename name. Copied clips keep their scheme when they are pasted, saved sessions hold the schemes, and Import Session Data brings them along. No readiness percentage change.

While the Strip Silence window is open, the Edit window draws a rectangle around each range that Strip would keep on the selected tracks, padded by Clip Start Pad and Clip End Pad, and the rectangles follow the sliders as they move. They are removed when the window closes. edit.stripsilencepreview returns the same ranges without changing the session. No readiness percentage change.

The Strip Silence window has a Rename button. It opens Rename Selected Clips, where a name, a starting number, a count of zeros and a suffix set the names of the clips that Strip, Extract and Separate leave in the selection (for example SFX023.Reel1, SFX024.Reel1). The app keeps the scheme for later uses of Strip Silence until the app quits, or until Clear and then OK empty it. No readiness percentage change.

The Strip Silence window has Extract and Separate buttons. Extract removes the audio and keeps the silent parts of the selection, and Separate separates the clips at the edges of the silence without removing anything. Minimum Strip Duration goes up to 4,000 ms. No readiness percentage change.

Clip › Loop… (Cmd+Alt+L) opens the Clip Looping dialog: Number of Loops, Loop Length in the main counter's time format, or Loop Until End of Session or Next Clip. A loop length that is not a whole number of loops cuts the last loop short, and Unloop removes that short loop too. No readiness percentage change.

AudioSuite ▸ Pitch Shift ▸ Vari-Fi slows the selected clips down to a complete stop or speeds them up from one, and the pitch follows the speed. Fit To keeps each clip's length and plays two-thirds of it; Extend plays all of it and makes the clip 150 % long. Fades On fades the audio out with the slowdown or in with the speedup. Before, the menu item resampled the clip at a constant speed. No readiness percentage change.

A built-in Auto Pan plugin pans the mono sum of a stereo track between left and right. An LFO with seven waveforms moves it at a rate in BPM or at the session tempo, running free, once, in step with the transport, or when the level crosses a threshold or a manual trigger changes; an envelope follower can move it by level instead. Width, Manual and Path set the field, and Output sets the level. No readiness percentage change.

A built-in Subharmonic (subharmonic) adds the octave below a lower and an upper band of the input, chosen from four frequency ranges, with a direct bass band, a gain and a solo for each band, Drive with six characters, HP and LP filters, and a Mix that keeps one path at full level. No readiness percentage change.

A built-in Ring Modulator (ringmod) applies ring modulation, frequency modulation or a positive or negative resonator, and an LFO, an envelope follower or sample and hold moves its frequency. AudioSuite › Modulation › Sci-Fi now runs it instead of the Flanger. No readiness percentage change.

Float32 WAV and AIFF-C encoding preserve finite samples above full scale. Integer PCM still clips at full scale. Tests cover whole-file and streaming encoders, non-finite samples, and bounce output with normalization on and off. No readiness percentage change.

Mono audio devices receive the average of the stereo channels before output clipping, retaining right-only audio. Surround mixes use the same average after their ITU stereo fold-down. Regression tests cover channel balance, polarity cancellation, clipping, centered mono tracks, each 5.1 channel and several callback sizes. No readiness percentage change.

Master fader volume automation uses each render block's actual last sample, matching track faders. Breakpoints in the next block no longer pull the preceding block's level toward them, and ramps reach their last-sample value. Regression tests cover nonzero starts, one-sample callbacks and several block sizes. No readiness percentage change.

Aux, folder and master latency calculations exclude inserts already taken out for producing NaN or infinity, matching audio tracks. Subsequent blocks no longer compensate for an insert that is bypassed after failure. Regression tests check impulse timing, healthy insert latency and reset/retry at 64- and 512-sample blocks. No readiness percentage change.

Split into Mono extracts the correct source channel for each mono track instead of playing channel zero on every track. Clip offsets, gain, fades and stretch, source timestamps, Undo/Redo and saved audio are preserved; repeated clips share each extracted mono source. Unavailable media returns an error without partial edits. No readiness percentage change.
MCP batch rejects more than 1000 calls before executing any command, instead of silently running only the first 1000 (#460). No readiness percentage change.

soundcraft-cli convert dithers only when the output loses resolution (fewer bits than the source, a float or lossy source, or resampled/normalized samples); a same-depth, wider or 32-bit float conversion copies the samples exactly and digital silence stays silent. --dither and --no-dither override the choice (#548)
WAV: an empty data chunk followed by metadata (LIST, bext) reads as no audio; a recording that was never finalised (sizes left at 0) still gives what was written (#466)

Sampler: a ping-pong loop keeps its phase and direction when a step is wider than the loop (a narrow loop with high transposition), instead of reflecting once and dropping the rest of the travel (#463)

(VST3 host messages): The VST3 host creates IMessage and IAttributeList objects for plugins (IHostApplication::createInstance), so plugins whose controller and processor talk through IConnectionPoint::notify work: Line 6 Helix Stadium Native now loads its content database (it reported "Failed to get content database recovery info (Out of memory condition)") and exposes its parameters. No readiness percentage change.

mix.instrument takes the built-in instrument's parameters in params (validated, clamped) and refuses any other field, so a synth setting written beside plugin is an error instead of being accepted and ignored (#265)

A bounce of a bus that an aux returns onto lines up with the timeline: the aux insert's lookahead is compensated like the main mix's (it left the bus late and cut the end off), and tracks routed to that bus wait for it too (#246)
Delay compensation covers the inserts of the master faders: a bounce of the main mix with a Maximizer on the master lines up with the same mix without it (it came out 71 samples late) (#351)

(audio device settings): Setup › Playback Engine chooses the audio system, output and input device, sample rate and buffer size, kept per machine with the preferences; 16/32-bit integer devices are converted; ASIO is available behind the opt-in asio build feature (verified with an SSL 2+ at 128 samples). Channel routing, one duplex clock and latency compensation remain (G-01). No readiness percentage change.

(Mix in a separate window): Window › Mix in Separate Window shows the Mix window in its own native window, so Edit and Mix can be on screen at once (e.g. one per monitor), as in Pro Tools. No readiness percentage change.

(plugin editors on Windows): VST3 editors and embedded CLAP editors open in a SoundCraft host window on Windows (owned by the app window, resized on request, closed from its title bar); verified with a JUCE VST3 compressor and a CLAP effect. No readiness percentage change.
soundcraft-cli convert rejects an unparsable or zero --rate and an unknown --bit-depth (exit 1, nothing written) instead of converting with a default (#256)
Timecode labels with huge fields no longer overflow: frame counts are computed in 128 bits and clamp, so setup.currenttimecode and session.formattime saturate instead of failing (#248)
session.formattime with the smallest bar number no longer fails with an internal error: the bar offset saturates (#249)

(plugin editors on Windows): VST3 editors and embedded CLAP editors open in a SoundCraft host window on Windows (owned by the app window, resized on request, closed from its title bar); verified with a JUCE VST3 compressor and a CLAP effect. No readiness percentage change.

(Mix in a separate window): Window › Mix in Separate Window shows the Mix window in its own native window, so Edit and Mix can be on screen at once (e.g. one per monitor), as in Pro Tools. No readiness percentage change.

(audio device settings): Setup › Playback Engine chooses the audio system, output and input device, sample rate and buffer size, kept per machine with the preferences; 16/32-bit integer devices are converted; ASIO is available behind the opt-in asio build feature (verified with an SSL 2+ at 128 samples). Channel routing, one duplex clock and latency compensation remain (G-01). No readiness percentage change.

(UI docking): Tracks and Groups, Clips, MIDI Editor, Memory Locations, and Undo History use movable panels. Edit and Mix retain separate arrangements; Clips and MIDI Editor belong to Edit. Transport, plug-in, and specialist utility windows retain their existing hosts. Panel moves and reset are available as UI commands, and saved UI preferences retain arrangements. Common toolbar and track record-enable buttons share interaction, accessible labels and keyboard focus through craft-ui, retaining blue tool selection and red record-arm states. No readiness percentage change.
— Stage re-normalized to pre-alpha by the core-workflow gate (interface recording, MIDI recording and session interchange fail). Full re-measure against Pro Tools Ultimate 2026.4.1 and the standard
— Light theme and live system appearance, clip-gain fader and nudge, missing-media

— Repository published; About window credits; release CI on macOS runners.
